reason: Both satisfy all hard requirements equally well (correct headings, snapshot-first mandate, explicit no-restart/failover-before-snapshot rule, and clear abort/rollback conditions), but Response A's MITIGATION section has more coherent risk-ordering logic, treating failover strictly as a last resort only if space reclamation fails and write failure is imminent. Response B's mitigation step 3 is internally confusing, proposing failover only after disk pressure is already relieved and latency is recovering, which undercuts the stated rationale of using failover to relieve load.
